Irene / Karthik — reviewed Helix's numbers and current fleet schedule. Short answer: we do not have an immediately available 16x-A100 contiguous pool for 04/01 without rebalancing existing Dedicated commitments. Current constraints:

- Q1 reserved capacity is ~92% committed across the US west region; we have a handful of pending rotations but not enough to free a 16x contiguous tranche by 04/01.
- Upcoming burst-heavy commitments for a different account (AuroraEdge) occupy the most flexible nodes through 03/28.

Options we can offer and tradeoffs:

1) Staggered activation (recommended): allocate 8x on 04/01 for core traffic and enable burst to 16x over two weeks as nodes free up. This requires Helix accept initial reduced concurrency and some routing logic in their release.
2) Hybrid pool + host fallback: create an isolated 8x dedicated pool and add automated routing to a host-shared high-throughput cluster for non-latency critical calls. Lower cost but increases tail-latency risk for some requests.
3) Priority swap (manual arbitration): Pause a non-SLA critical customer's scheduled burst for 10 days and reassign that capacity to Helix. This will require leadership sign-off since it impacts revenue fairness and might trigger credits.

If leadership wants to prioritize Helix immediately we need a decision and a replacement plan for the affected account. I estimate operational effort ~6 engineer-days to reconfigure routing and KV cache for a staggered rollout.

Marcus Lin
Head of Capacity Planning | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Daniel Park <daniel.park@helixsys.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 16:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Escalation: decision required for HLX-339 capacity allocation

Monica — need quick guidance. Helix (HLX-339) expects production on 04/01 and is a strategic expansion (20% ACV increase on existing account). Marcus outlined three options; option 3 (priority swap) would get them full 16x immediately but impacts another customer (AuroraEdge) with a predictable short-term credit exposure (~$23k) and operational churn. Option 1 (stagger) reduces near-term risk but forces Helix to delay some features.

Below are decision levers:
- Approve priority swap and accept credit/ops impact (explicitly authorize Marcus to reassign nodes).
- Approve staggered activation and commit Redwood engineering support for a two-week ramp (we tell Helix to soft-launch non-critical endpoints first).
- Offer hybrid fallback and include a startup credit plus a SLA amendment to mitigate latency risk.

Recommendation: staggered activation (Option 1) + 30% launch credit to Helix to cover missing capacity while nodes rotate back in. This keeps fairness intact and avoids escalating customer credits across the board.

Daniel — please confirm whether Helix can accept an 8x start on 04/01 with ramping to 16x over the following 10 business days. If not, flag now and we will escalate to swap.

Karthik Iyer
VP, Sales
